answer: Trust propagates from anchored identities through degree-normalized random walks capped at \(t\) steps, so each node’s score reflects reachable walk mass. A sybil cluster with sparse external edges has low conductance: little mass crosses its cut, bounding its aggregate vote for fixed seed weight and walk horizon. A nadir threshold can flag isolated mass; the conductance ledge is a risk boundary, not proof of identity. Jade-marked nodes receive no special trust.
